summary_en: CCI Group raised its FY2027 annual dividend forecast to 35 yen per share from 30 yen, an increase of 5 yen, reflecting upward revision of net profit attributable to parent company to 19.0 billion yen on higher interest income at subsidiary Hokuriku Bank and lower tax burden.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Full-Year Consolidated Earnings Forecast and Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase) for Fiscal Year Ending March 2027
translation_en_brief:
CCI Group announced on October 30, 2026, that it has revised its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The annual dividend per share has been increased to 35 yen from the previously announced 30 yen, representing a 5 yen increase. The interim dividend remains at 15 yen per share, while the year-end dividend has been raised to 20 yen per share, up 5 yen from the previous forecast of 15 yen.

The dividend increase follows an upward revision of the company's full-year consolidated earnings forecast. Net profit attributable to the parent company has been raised to 19.0 billion yen from 17.0 billion yen, driven by increased interest income at Hokuriku Bank, the company's consolidated subsidiary, benefiting from rising interest rates, and a lower effective tax rate due to tax accounting effects. Operating profit remains unchanged at 26.5 billion yen.

The revision aligns with the company's shareholder return policy targeting a dividend payout ratio of approximately 40%, with the revised forecast resulting in a payout ratio of 40.6% for the fiscal year ending March 2027.
